items.actual_relevant_use_quote:
Use SI constants $G_N>0$ in $\mathrm{m^3\,kg^{-1}\,s^{-2}}$, $c>0$ in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $\hbar>0$ in $\mathrm{J\,s}$, and $k_B>0$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$. In [[prop-tgr-ideal-evaporation-accounting]], the mathematical constant $G$ is identified with this same $G_N$.

For each fixed mass $M>0$ in kilograms, take the zero-angular-momentum, zero-charge member of the selected Kerr–Newman stationary family [[pthm-tgr-kn-family-mechanics]], with geometric mass length $m=G_NM/c^2$ in metres. In the Schwarzschild exterior use coordinates $(x^0,r,\vartheta,\varphi)$, $x^0=ct_\infty$ in metres, $r>2m$, and metric
$$
ds^2=-\left(1-\frac{2m}{r}\right)(dx^0)^2+ \left(1-\frac{2m}{r}\right)^{-1}dr^2+r^2d\Omega_2^2,
$$
where $d\Omega_2^2$ is the unit-sphere metric. The asymptotic generator is $\xi=\partial_{x^0}$, with $g(\xi,\xi)\to-1$ at infinity. The selected stationary-family radius, area, and geometric surface gravity are
$$
r_H(M)=2m=\frac{2G_NM}{c^2},\qquad A_H(M)=4\pi r_H(M)^2,\qquad \kappa_{\rm geom}(M)=\frac{1}{4m}=\frac{c^2}{4G_NM}.
$$
Thus $r_H$ is in metres, $A_H$ in $\mathrm{m^2}$, and $\kappa_{\rm geom}$ in $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$, using the length-normalized generator convention of [[def-tgr-framework-units]].

Adopt the selected reduced-model reference temperature from [[post-tgr-thermodynamic-horizon-identification]] on this Schwarzschild subfamily:
$$
T_\infty(M):=T_K=T_{\rm red} =\frac{\hbar c\kappa_{\rm geom}(M)}{2\pi k_B} =\frac{\hbar c^3}{8\pi G_NMk_B}>0.
$$
This is an adopted model identification for one fixed asymptotic reference. It is not a local proper-temperature field and does not assert a general Hawking state. The reversible entropy state $S_H$ is the value of the stationary-family state function on each Schwarzschild member; evaluating that family function along a changing parameter $M(t_\infty)$ is bookkeeping in this model, not a claim that the changing family is an exact spacetime solution.

Adopt the zero-mode-excluded, zero-point-subtracted, two-polarization photon Gibbs model and isotropic freely streaming ray convention of [[thm-tgr-photon-planck-flux]], under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ from [[def-countable-choice]]. Its energy density $u$, coarse diagonal-mode entropy density $s$, and one-sided fluxes are those of that theorem. This identification is an ideal reservoir assumption; no photon-wall equilibration theorem or physical preparation is asserted.

Fix $0<\eta\leq1$, a constant dimensionless active-area fraction, an initial mass $M_0>0$, and a positive cutoff $0<M_{\min}<M_0$. Let $M(t_\infty)>0$ be $C^1$ on an interval containing its first cutoff time $\tau$, with $M(0)=M_0$, and let $t_\infty$ be measured in seconds by the fixed asymptotic time parameter. Define $E_\infty(t_\infty)=M(t_\infty)c^2$ in joules and the effective far-field emitting area
$$
A_{\rm eff}(M):=\eta A_H(M).
$$
Adopt zero incoming flux, the power law $P_\infty=A_{\rm eff}\sigma T_\infty^4$ in watts, the balance equation
$$
\frac{dE_\infty}{dt_\infty}=c^2M'(t_\infty)=-P_\infty(t_\infty),
$$
and the coarse exported entropy rate $S_{\rm rad}'=(4/3)P_\infty/T_\infty$, with $S_{\rm rad}(0)=0$. Here $S_{\rm rad}$ is the entropy carried by the ideal Gibbs/ray model, not an outside von Neumann entropy. The effective area is not a material patch of the null horizon and $\eta$ is not a frequency-independent greybody factor applied separately to entropy.

The model holds only for the fixed normalization $\xi$. Under $\xi\mapsto b\xi$, $b>0$, the model conventions scale $E_\xi\mapsto bE_\xi$, $t_\xi\mapsto t_\xi/b$, $\kappa_{\rm geom}\mapsto b\kappa_{\rm geom}$, and leave $A_H$ unchanged. The Stefan closure above is therefore not stipulated as a reference-independent luminosity law. No experiment, coupled backreaction solution, physical extinction event, or universal generalized second law is adopted.

actual_proof_quotes.1.1: The outgoing one-sided flux in [F2] and the adopted area/temperature in [F1] give $P_\infty=\eta A_H\sigma T_\infty^4$. Substituting $A_H=16\pi G_N^2M^2/c^4$, $T_\infty=\hbar c^3/(8\pi G_NMk_B)$, and $\sigma=\pi^2k_B^4/(60\hbar^3c^2)$ yields $P_\infty=\eta\hbar c^6/(15360\pi G_N^2M^2)$. The adopted balance equation is therefore $M'=-\alpha M^{-2}$ with $\alpha=\eta\hbar c^4/(15360\pi G_N^2)>0$. [given, F1, F2, A2, algebra]
actual_proof_quotes.1.2: The hypotheses of [F3] match the fixed-reference area, temperature, outgoing flux, mass-balance law, and strictly positive cutoff in [F1]. Its exact solution gives the displayed $M(t_\infty)$, $\tau$, and energy export. No continuation to $M=0$ is used. [given, F1, F3, A2]
actual_proof_quotes.1.3: Put $m=G_NM/c^2$, $a=q=0$. Since $m>0$, this point lies in the strict subextremal domain of [L1]; the selected Schwarzschild horizon area is the same $A_H=16\pi G_N^2M^2/c^4$ used by [F1] and [F3]. Therefore [L1] gives $S_H(M)=k_Bc^3A_H(M)/(4G_N\hbar)+s_*$, while [F3] gives $S_B(M)=k_Bc^3A_H(M)/(4G_N\hbar)+S_0$. Their constant offsets may differ, but subtracting the values at $M_0$ and $M_{\min}$ cancels each offset and gives $S_H(M_0)-S_H(M_{\min})=S_B(M_0)-S_B(M_{\min})>0$, because $M_0>M_{\min}>0$. The $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ assumption [A2] is carried for the reduced-spectrum input in [L1]. [given, F1, F3, L1, A1, A2, algebra]
actual_proof_quotes.1.4: The definition [F4] and ODE of [F3] give $\epsilon_{\rm qs}=|M'|(2G_NM/c^3)/M=2G_N\alpha/(c^3M^2)$. Since $M\geq M_{\min}$, the supremum is the displayed positive-cutoff value; the threshold follows by multiplying by $M_{\min}^2>0$. The exact finite-interval ratio and bound are [F5]. These are internal properties of the stipulated ODE. [F3, F4, F5, A2, algebra]
actual_proof_quotes.2.1: By [F3], $S_{\rm rad}(\tau)=(4/3)[S_B(M_0)-S_B(M_{\min})]$. Step 1.3 replaces this difference by $\Delta S_H$. Thus $S_{\rm rad}(\tau)=(4/3)\Delta S_H$, and $S_H(M_{\min})+S_{\rm rad}(\tau)-S_H(M_0)=-(\Delta S_H)+(4/3)\Delta S_H=(1/3)\Delta S_H>0$. This is the stated coarse model entropy accounting only. [F3, step 1.3, A2, algebra]
actual_proof_quotes.3.1: Under the rescaling $\xi_b=b\xi$, the energy $E_\xi=-c\,p_a\xi^a$ scales by $b$, the normalized time parameter scales as $t_b=t_\infty/b$, and the geometric surface gravity scales as $\kappa_b=b\kappa_{\rm geom}$. Hence $P_b=dE_b/dt_b=b^2P_\infty$, while $T_b=\hbar c\kappa_b/(2\pi k_B)=bT_\infty$, so $A_{\rm eff}\sigma T_b^4=b^4A_{\rm eff}\sigma T_\infty^4$ with unchanged area and coefficient. The equality stipulated in [F1] therefore belongs to its fixed normalization and cannot be reused unchanged for arbitrary $b$. [F1, algebra] ∎

actual_proof_quotes.1.1:
With $\eta=1$, [F1] gives $\alpha=\hbar c^4/(15360\pi G_N^2)$. Hence $t_*=M_0^3/(3\alpha)=5120\pi G_N^2M_0^3/(\hbar c^4)$, and
$$
\tau=\frac{M_0^3-(M_0/2)^3}{3\alpha} =\left(1-\frac18\right)t_*=\frac78t_*.
$$
The cutoff remains positive, $M(\tau)=M_0/2$, so the model does not reach its algebraic zero-mass time. [given, F1, A1, A2, algebra]
actual_proof_quotes.1.2: The energy export in [F1] is $c^2(M_0-M_{\min})$. Substituting [A1] gives $c^2M_0/2$ joules. [F1, A1, A2, algebra]
actual_proof_quotes.1.3: By [F1], $S_H(M)=4\pi k_BG_NM^2/(\hbar c)+s_*$ on the selected branch, with an unfixed constant $s_*$. Subtracting its values at $M_0$ and $M_0/2$ cancels $s_*$ and gives $\Delta S_H=4\pi k_BG_N(3M_0^2/4)/(\hbar c)=3\pi k_BG_NM_0^2/(\hbar c)$. The entropy export is $4\Delta S_H/3=4\pi k_BG_NM_0^2/(\hbar c)$, and the total gain is $\Delta S_H/3=\pi k_BG_NM_0^2/(\hbar c)$. [given, F1, A1, A2, algebra]
actual_proof_quotes.2.1:
The maximum diagnostic occurs at $M=M_{\min}=M_0/2$, so [F1] gives
$$
\epsilon_{\rm qs,max}=\frac{2G_N\alpha}{c^3(M_0/2)^2} =\frac{8G_N\alpha}{c^3M_0^2} =\frac{\hbar c}{1920\pi G_NM_0^2}.
$$
The displayed lower bound on $M_0^2$ is equivalent, after multiplication by the positive $1920\pi G_NM_0^2\epsilon_0/(\hbar c)$, to $\epsilon_{\rm qs,max}\leq\epsilon_0$. This remains an internal diagnostic for the stipulated ODE, not a comparison with a coupled spacetime solution. [F1, A1, A2, algebra] ∎
